title: Price a voyage
lead: Choose a route and a dated market. Every field starts from its source or says why it is empty, and every change prices the voyage again with the same engine as the rest of the study.

words.verdict: At these inputs the voyage earns {tce} a day over {days} days.
words.verdict_trip: At this hire the owner earns {tce} a day over {days} days, the ballast leg back to the delivery area included; over the {trip_days} days of the trip alone the hire nets {trip_tce} a day after commission.
words.verdict_negative: At these inputs the voyage loses {tce} a day over {days} days.
words.published: The Baltic published {published} for this week; the engine reads {error} percent {direction}.
words.no_freight: Enter a freight rate under Market to price the voyage.
words.ws_missing: The rate is in Worldscale points, and a Worldscale rate needs the route's flat rate in USD a tonne. Flat rates are licensed by the Worldscale Association and no public source states this route's for the year: enter it under Market, or switch the freight to USD a tonne or a lump sum.
words.leaves_out: The TCE leaves out {items}, so with them it would be lower.
words.leaves_out_none: Every voyage cost of this voyage has a figure.
words.estimate: A TCE is an estimate of what a voyage earns at stated inputs, not a forecast.
words.breakeven_heading: Freight that earns a TCE of
words.breakeven_target_unit: USD a day; zero gives the freight that only covers voyage costs
words.bridge_title: Where the freight goes: {gross} of freight, {result} left after commission and {costs} of voyage costs.
words.bridge_caption: The bridge from gross freight to the voyage result, in US dollars, one row per step.
words.tornado_title: {first} moves the TCE most: {range} a day between its two cases.
words.tornado_desc: Each bar runs from the TCE with the input lower to the TCE with it higher; the base TCE is the vertical rule.
words.speed_title: The TCE is highest at {best} knots laden at these inputs; the voyage is priced at {current}.
words.speed_title_bound: The TCE still rises at {best} knots, the top of the range the published consumptions support; the voyage is priced at {current}.
words.speed_axis_x: Laden speed, knots (ballast keeps its gap)
words.speed_desc: The TCE at each laden speed from one knot below the slowest published consumption to one knot above the fastest. Between published pairs consumption is interpolated; outside them it follows the power law fitted to the pairs.
words.speed_title_low: The TCE is highest at {best} knots, the slowest speed searched; the voyage is priced at {current}.
words.speed_trip_note: On a trip the hire is paid by the day and the charterer buys the laden fuel, so a faster ship shortens the paid days and the owner's TCE falls with speed.
words.source: Engine output at the inputs above. Preset: {preset}; bunkers and carbon: {market}.
words.result_line: Over {days} days ({ballast} in ballast, {laden} laden and {port} in port and waiting), the result is a TCE of {tce} a day.
words.routing_note: A routing sets the leg's distance and its miles inside ECAs; canal days and tolls stay as entered.
words.ets_year_note: 40 percent of 2024 emissions, 70 percent of 2025 and 100 percent from 2026, with methane and nitrous oxide from 2026 (Directive 2003/87/EC, Articles 3gb and 3ga).
words.scrubber: Scrubber fitted: burns HSFO outside ECAs
words.scrubber_in_eca: Scrubber also used inside ECAs, where local rules allow
words.fueleu: Include the FuelEU Maritime penalty in the TCE
words.curve_fit: Outside the published pairs consumption follows c = a v^b fitted to them: laden b {laden}, ballast b {ballast}.
words.not_cited: A scenario input: the base case uses the value shown.
words.data_caption: Every input of the voyage as it now stands, with its status and its source.
method: The calculator runs src/engine.js, the browser copy of the Python engine, checked against it to within one part in a billion on every committed test case. The TCE is gross freight and other revenue less commission and voyage costs, divided by the days of the whole round voyage, ballast leg included. On a trip charter the owner's TCE is the hire over the trip less commission, less the costs the owner bears (the ballast leg's bunkers and allowances), over the trip and the ballast leg.

Steaming days are distance over speed times 24 hours, plus the weather margin. Fuel at sea follows the ship's published speed and consumption pairs, interpolated between them and extended outside them by a power law fitted to them; inside an emission control area the ship burns MGO, outside VLSFO, or HSFO behind a scrubber. The sensitivities change one input at a time and keep the others.

war_risk_rates.area: Red Sea and Bab el Mandeb
war_risk_rates.quote: Even during the attacks by the Houthis rebels in Yemen on ships in the Red Sea and the Bab al-Mandab Strait, in 2024, the AWRP rarely reached 1% of the H&M value. Most of the time, it remained between 0.4% and 0.7%
war_risk_rates.reported: Platts, quoting two maritime insurance brokers, republished by Hellenic Shipping News on 1 April 2026

war_risk_rates.quote: Premiums for vessels transiting the Bab al-Mandab Strait currently stand at 0.5% of hull value, according to Baker
war_risk_rates.reported: Marsh (Marcus Baker) to Platts, 22 July 2026, republished by Hellenic Shipping News on 24 July 2026

war_risk_rates.quote: in the pre-war period, when the value was around 0.1%-0.15%, or even lower, two maritime insurers said

war_risk_rates.quote: European tanker sources put the figure closer to 7%-9% for clean tankers and 5%-5.75% for crude tankers
